gita-fun-electronics-kids-zugdidi.about:
GITA's Zugdidi Technopark runs practical, interactive electronics workshops (registered as 'Fun Electronics') for children aged 9-12. Through games and experiments, children learn to assemble circuits, connect components and build simple electronic devices.

Each workshop lasts two days and is free; GITA states that all its programmes are free of charge. Parents register the child through the online questionnaire and wait for a call.

Designed to spark early interest in technology and give younger children their first hands-on electronics experience.
highlights: Free, ages 9-12
Learning through play and experiments
Build a first electronic device
gita-fun-electronics-kids-zugdidi.eligibility: Children aged 9-12; aimed at families in Zugdidi and Samegrelo. Georgian-language.

gita-lego-spike-little-inventors-zugdidi.about:
Little Inventors is a LEGO SPIKE robotics course at GITA's Zugdidi Technopark in Samegrelo. Students aged 13-15 learn the basics of robotics and programming, build and program their own robots, and work with sensors and mechanisms through practical tasks that develop logical and creative thinking.

The course is free. After registering on the GITA questionnaire, applicants receive a call with the schedule.

A good starting point for school robotics teams and for pupils curious about engineering.
highlights: Free, ages 13-15
Build and program your own robot
Run by GITA's Zugdidi Technopark
gita-lego-spike-little-inventors-zugdidi.eligibility: Ages 13-15; aimed at pupils in Zugdidi and Samegrelo. Georgian-language.

Attend the sessions at the technopark

gita-lego-spike-robotics-workshop-gurjaa.about:
GITA's Gurjaani Technopark runs a LEGO Education SPIKE robotics workshop for children and teenagers aged 10 and over. Participants assemble mechanisms from LEGO parts, work with sensors and motors, learn basic block-based programming, and then design their own interactive robots to complete tasks.

The workshop lasts three days and follows a learning-by-doing approach. Sessions are held in rounds so that everyone who registers gets a place; GITA sends each registrant the exact schedule by SMS and email.

It is a free first step into robotics for pupils in Kakheti, and a natural lead-in to FIRST LEGO League-style competitions.
highlights: Free, ages 10+
Sensors, motors and block coding with LEGO SPIKE
Rolling rounds so all registrants get a slot
gita-lego-spike-robotics-workshop-gurjaa.eligibility: Children and teenagers aged 10+; aimed at residents of Gurjaani and Kakheti. Georgian-language.
how_to_apply: Open the programme page on gita.gov.ge
Click through to the registration questionnaire on apps.mygita.ge and fill it in
Wait for GITA's call, SMS or email with the exact schedule
Attend the sessions at the technopark
gita-lego-spike-robotics-workshop-gurjaa.costs: Free (GITA technopark programmes are free of charge).

gita-market-hack-gurjaani-2026.about:
Market Hack is a marketing-themed hackathon organised by GITA at its Gurjaani Technopark in Kakheti. Participants develop technological and innovative solutions to challenges in the marketing sector, with mentors and the technopark's FabLab helping turn ideas into prototypes.

The topic and research findings are announced remotely on 6 November 2026; on 7-8 November participants work on site in Gurjaani with mentoring, prototyping, final presentations and awards. You can enter alone or in a team of 2-4 (each member registers separately). Up to 65 participants are selected and only selected applicants are contacted. Round-trip transport between Tbilisi and Gurjaani is provided.

The author of the best project receives a 10,000 GEL grant to develop the prototype, which makes this one of the better-rewarded youth hackathons in Georgia.
highlights: 10,000 GEL grant for the winning project
Free transport from Tbilisi
Mentors and FabLab prototyping
gita-market-hack-gurjaani-2026.eligibility: Ages 16+, from anywhere in Georgia; individuals or teams of 2-4. Working language Georgian.
how_to_apply: Open the Market Hack page on gita.gov.ge
Each team member fills in the registration questionnaire on apps.mygita.ge by 1 November 2026
Wait to be contacted if selected (up to 65 participants)
Join the remote kick-off on 6 November and come to Gurjaani on 7-8 November
gita-market-hack-gurjaani-2026.costs: Free; transport Tbilisi-Gurjaani-Tbilisi provided. Prize: 10,000 GEL grant.

gita-restart-revive-ozurgeti-2026.about:
Re:Start - Re:Vive is a hands-on STEAM week run by GITA at the Ozurgeti Technopark in Guria. Participants re-evaluate, improve and develop ideas from earlier projects and hackathons; past winners take part and newcomers join existing teams to work on real-world problems, with the goal of producing 10-12 technology prototypes.

The programme starts on 5 November 2026 and lasts five days. It is open to anyone aged 14 and over, needs no prior experience, and has 50 places. Participation is free and meals and transport are provided.

A good entry point for school pupils who want real prototyping experience and a team to join, without having to bring their own idea.
highlights: Free, with meals and transport
Join an existing team; no experience required
Goal: 10-12 working prototypes
gita-restart-revive-ozurgeti-2026.eligibility: Anyone aged 14+ (mainly young people from Guria and western Georgia). Georgian-language.

Wait for GITA's call, SMS or email with the exact schedule
Attend the sessions at the technopark

gita-snap-circuits-electronics-workshop-.about:
This GITA workshop at the Gurjaani Technopark introduces electronics through the Snap Circuits Extreme STEM kit. Participants build simple circuits, learn how electric current, sensors and basic components work, and assemble their own small electronic devices.

The workshop lasts two days, is aimed at ages 12 and over and is free. Registrants receive the exact dates by SMS and email.

A practical, low-barrier introduction to electronics for pupils who may later move on to Arduino, robotics or engineering.
highlights: Free, ages 12+
Hands-on circuits with Snap Circuits kits
Build your own small device
gita-snap-circuits-electronics-workshop-.eligibility: Ages 12+; aimed at young people in Gurjaani and Kakheti. Georgian-language.

gita-tech-talk-giorgi-danelia-gurjaani-2.about:
GITA's Gurjaani Technopark hosts a Tech Talk with Giorgi Danelia, a Georgian video-blogger and businessman who founded GD Squad and GD Tech. The talk covers modern technologies and their practical use, development trends, marketing and digital content creation.

It is open to school students aged 15+, university students and anyone interested in tech, marketing and content creation. Only the first 90 registered participants can attend.
highlights: Meet a well-known Georgian tech creator
Learn about content creation and tech marketing
Free, 15+
gita-tech-talk-giorgi-danelia-gurjaani-2.eligibility: School students aged 15+, university students and adults interested in technology and digital content.
how_to_apply: Register via the GITA form (apps.mygita.ge/zs/1tDBlj)
Arrive at Gurjaani Technopark on 3 Nov at 14:00

gori-university-student-conference-2026.about:
Gori State University (Shida Kartli) holds its fifth International Student Scientific Conference, 'Education and Innovation', on 10 December 2026. It runs in hybrid mode: in person at the university in Gori and online via Zoom. Each participant presents one paper (alone or with up to two co-authors) both orally and as a poster, and receives a certificate.

Sections: education and pedagogy; mathematics and informatics; exact and natural sciences; business, economics and tourism; social sciences and law; philology; history; sport and sport management. Papers of up to 12 A4 pages (Georgian, English or Russian) follow APA style and include an English abstract of up to 300 words and 4-5 keywords; a programme committee selects the talks.

A low-barrier first conference for undergraduates who want a presentation and a certificate on their CV; no registration fee.
highlights: No registration fee; online participation possible
Open to bachelor's and master's students from any country
Eight subject sections; certificate for presenters
gori-university-student-conference-2026.eligibility: Bachelor's and master's students of universities in Georgia or abroad. One paper per participant, with at most two co-authors. Working languages: Georgian, English, Russian.
how_to_apply: Download the application form and information letter from the conference page on gu.edu.ge
Write your paper (max 12 pages, APA style, English abstract of up to 300 words, 4-5 keywords)
Email the completed form and the paper (.doc, named by surname) to conference@gu.edu.ge by 20 November 2026
If selected, present orally and with a poster on 10 December, in Gori or via Zoom
gori-university-student-conference-2026.costs: Free. The university covers conference costs; travel and accommodation are not reimbursed.

gtu-erasmus-exchange-fall-2027.about:
Georgian Technical University (GTU) has Erasmus+ agreements with many European universities and announces each mobility as a separate competition on its 'Current Contests' page, stating the field, level, number of places and deadlines. Recent student calls included Mining/Geology/Petroleum at the University of Zagreb (2 places, 5 months), Business at Wittenborg UAS (7 places, with a 2-week internship), Business/IS/Finance/Architecture at the University of Liechtenstein, Architecture at ENSA Normandie (4 places), Food Science at Junia ISA Lille (2 master's places), Business/Economics at UMCS Lublin and Sapienza Rome.

Selection involves document submission, a foreign-language test and an interview with the competition committee; nominated students then register with the host university. Most mobilities carry an Erasmus+ grant (some are zero-grant). Fall-semester calls closed in March-April in 2026, so expect fall 2027 calls in spring 2027; GTU also runs weekly Erasmus+ consultations.
highlights: Partner-specific calls across Europe
Language test + interview selection
Fall 2027 calls expected Mar-Apr 2027
gtu-erasmus-exchange-fall-2027.eligibility: Students enrolled at Georgian Technical University in the field and level named in each call (bachelor's, master's or PhD).
how_to_apply: Monitor gtu.edu.ge 'Current Contests' (Erasmus+)
Attend GTU's weekly Erasmus+ consultations
Submit documents by the call deadline
Take the foreign-language test and interview
If nominated, apply on the host university's platform
gtu-erasmus-exchange-fall-2027.costs: Erasmus+ grant (travel + monthly allowance) where stated; some calls are zero-grant; host tuition waived.

gtu-named-and-rmg-scholarships-2027.about:
Georgian Technical University (GTU) in Tbilisi offers several scholarships for motivated, successful students: faculty named scholarships (Niko Nikoladze, David Sarajishvili, Akaki Khoshtaria), the Zviad Gamsakhurdia presidential scholarship for law and related students, the RMG Scholarship Programme from the largest mining company in the South Caucasus (to discover and support motivated engineering students), Green Scholarships under the programme on climate-related disaster risk reduction in Georgia, the Tamaz Bekaia Educational Foundation scholarship, and the state programme 'State Scholarships for Students' (GEL 150 per month per semester at state universities).

These stack with UNE state grants and help engineering students cover living costs.
highlights: Industry-funded RMG scholarship for engineering students
Named faculty and 'green' climate scholarships
State stipend for successful students
gtu-named-and-rmg-scholarships-2027.eligibility: Students enrolled at GTU meeting each scholarship's academic and field criteria (e.g. engineering majors for RMG).
how_to_apply: Enrol at GTU (via the Unified National Exams for bachelor's).
Watch GTU's scholarships page and faculty announcements each semester.
Apply with your transcript and documents required by each scholarship.
gtu-named-and-rmg-scholarships-2027.costs: Varies by scholarship: monthly stipends or one-off awards; state scholarship GEL 150/month.

ibsu-american-studies-for-school-student.about:
IBSU's American Studies training, billed as 'a chance to travel to America', introduces school pupils to the United States: its global influence, history and culture, everyday modern American life, and relations between the US and Georgia.

The sessions are run on the IBSU campus in Tbilisi by successful students of the university's American Studies programme, and mix short talks with themed, game-style activities so participants apply what they learn. The registration form accepts pupils in grades 9 to 12.

It is a light, low-pressure way to test an interest in international relations, American culture or English-language study before choosing a university programme.
highlights: Introduction to US history, culture and society
Led by IBSU American Studies students
Interactive themed activities on campus
ibsu-american-studies-for-school-student.eligibility: Secondary-school pupils in Georgia (the form asks for a Georgian personal number). Sessions are run in Georgian on the IBSU campus in Tbilisi.
how_to_apply: Open the programme page on ibsu.edu.ge
Fill in the registration form (name, email, Georgian personal number, phone, school, grade)
Tick the two consent boxes and press 'Send' (გაგზავნა)
Wait for IBSU to contact you with the schedule
ibsu-american-studies-for-school-student.costs: The page does not state a fee; IBSU's school-pupil projects are normally free.

ibsu-art-of-negotiation-school-students.about:
The Art of Negotiation (მოლაპარაკების ხელოვნება) is a school-pupil training led by IBSU lecturer Davit Bragvadze, who draws on years of experience in conflict management.

The first part covers proven rules and methods of problem solving, techniques used by diplomats, and etiquette and professional standards. The second part includes a themed film screening, a discussion and other activities. The registration form accepts pupils in grades 9 to 12; sessions are held on the IBSU campus in Tbilisi in Georgian.

It pairs well with Model UN and debate: students learn how real negotiators prepare, frame and close a deal.
highlights: Taught by a conflict-management lecturer
Diplomatic negotiation techniques and etiquette
Film screening and discussion

ibsu-ask-the-psychologist-school-student.about:
Ask the Psychologist (ჰკითხე ფსიქოლოგს) is a free IBSU project for pupils in grades 10, 11 and 12. It is led by Teona Guburiani, head of IBSU's psychology programme, together with successful psychology students.

The session starts with fun group activities and continues with an open discussion in which pupils ask questions on topics that interest them and get detailed answers. It takes place on the IBSU campus in Tbilisi and is run in Georgian.

It is a relaxed introduction to psychology as a subject and a career, useful for students weighing up social-science degrees.
highlights: Free; grades 10-12
Led by the head of IBSU's psychology programme
Open Q&A with psychologists

ibsu-business-alphabet-school-students.about:
Business Alphabet (ბიზნეს ანბანი) is a free student-run project of the IBSU Business School that aims to deepen school pupils' understanding of business. Participants get short introductions to marketing, finance, accounting, management and tourism.

The trainings are prepared and delivered by IBSU business students on the university campus in Tbilisi. The project has run since 2014 and, according to IBSU, more than 5,000 pupils have taken part. It is aimed at pupils in grades 10, 11 and 12.

It is a good first step for anyone considering business, economics or tourism at university, and a useful line for a CV or application.
highlights: Free since 2014, 5,000+ past participants
Marketing, finance, accounting, management and tourism

ibsu-economind-school-students.about:
EconoMind is listed among International Black Sea University's trainings for school pupils (ტრენინგები მოსწავლეებისთვის). As its name suggests it is an economics-themed project; the page itself gives only the title and the registration form, which accepts pupils in grades 9 to 12.

Like IBSU's other school projects it runs on the Tbilisi campus in Georgian, and the university contacts registered pupils with the schedule. Call IBSU on +995 322 800 064 (Mon-Fri 9:00-18:00) for details on content and dates.

A low-effort way to get a first taste of economics in a university setting.

ibsu-geopolitical-games-school-students.about:
Geopolitical Games (გეოპოლიტიკური თამაშები) is a free IBSU project that combines theory with a practical competition. Participants study international relations as a discipline, diplomacy as a profession, the lives of the 'fathers of diplomacy' and how international relations are actually conducted.

The practical part is a themed competition held in the university grounds. The project is led by Nino Samkharadze, lecturer in IBSU's International Relations programme, with IR students; it is aimed at pupils in grades 10-12 and runs in Georgian in Tbilisi.

Ideal for students drawn to MUN, diplomacy or IR degrees who want a competitive, hands-on introduction.

ibsu-internal-grants-2027.about:
International Black Sea University, a private English-language university in Tbilisi, offers internal grants to students admitted through the Unified National Exams. TOP 50 grant: 50% for the top 50 of all students admitted to IBSU by UNE score; TOP 51–150 grant: 25%; Gold medal grant: 50% for school gold medallists; First-priority grant: 20% for applicants who list IBSU first; Creative tour grant for architecture and graphic design applicants who pass IBSU's creative tour.

Where a student qualifies for more than one grant, the highest applies. Grants are kept by meeting the university's annual academic condition. All these grants are open to every applicant who chooses IBSU.
highlights: 50% tuition for top 50 entrants and gold medallists
25% for ranks 51–150; 20% for choosing IBSU first
English-taught programmes in Tbilisi
ibsu-internal-grants-2027.eligibility: Applicants admitted to an IBSU bachelor's programme through the 2027 Unified National Exams.
how_to_apply: Register for the Unified National Exams in spring 2027.
Put IBSU as first priority to secure at least the 20% grant.
Architecture/graphic design applicants: pass IBSU's creative tour.
Grants are applied on enrolment; meet the yearly academic condition to keep them.
ibsu-internal-grants-2027.costs: Tuition reductions of 20%, 25% or 50% (creative-tour grant per programme rules); combinable with the state grant.

ibsu-journalism-for-school-students.about:
IBSU's Journalism for School Students is a free training covering four topics: journalism as a profession, journalism ethics, preparing a news story, and methods for verifying information.

Alongside the sessions, participants take part in practical activities and learn to use IBSU's own television and radio facilities on the Tbilisi campus. The training is open to pupils in grades 9 to 12.

It suits students who write for a school paper, run social media, or are thinking about media, communications or political science at university.
highlights: Free; grades 9-12
Ethics, news writing and fact-checking
Hands-on time in IBSU's TV and radio studios

ibsu-project-management-school-students.about:
IBSU's Project Management training offers pupils in grades 11 and 12 a practical introduction to how projects are planned and delivered. Participants learn to plan and manage a project, work effectively in a team, use their time well and present their ideas, and then practise on real projects.

The training is free, runs in Georgian on the IBSU campus in Tbilisi and is coordinated by IBSU students.

The skills transfer directly to school clubs, volunteering, startup competitions and university applications that ask for evidence of initiative.
highlights: Free; grades 11-12
Planning, teamwork, time management, presenting
Practice on real projects

ibsu-state-organization-school-students.about:
State Organisation (სახელმწიფო მოწყობა) is a free IBSU project for pupils in grades 10, 11 and 12. Participants learn the main characteristics of a state, state symbols, forms and systems of government, the separation of powers, economic organisation, local self-government and international relations.

They then apply this in practical, game-like tasks, including creating their own states. The project is led by lecturer Ana Gogoladze with IBSU International Relations students and runs in Georgian on the Tbilisi campus.

Useful preparation for civics olympiads, Model UN and law or political-science degrees.
highlights: Free; grades 10-12
Design-your-own-state simulation
Led by an IBSU International Relations lecturer

iec-doctoral-studies-abroad-grant-2027.about:
The International Education Center (IEC) runs the state programme 'Support for doctoral-level education abroad' each academic year. Georgian citizens apply in a first stage with their profile and research plan, then submit proof of admission and tuition/research funding needs in a second stage.

The grant cannot be combined with other European or state funding (Erasmus+, Erasmus Mundus etc.) for the same studies. Grant holders must return and work in Georgia after graduation, although they may stay abroad for up to one year after completing their studies under the programme rules.
highlights: State funding for a full PhD abroad
Two-stage application: profile, then admission documents
Part of Georgia's flagship IEC programmes
iec-doctoral-studies-abroad-grant-2027.eligibility: Citizens of Georgia (or holders of Georgian status-neutral documents) with a master's degree, applying to or admitted to a doctoral programme at an eligible foreign university; must accept the return-and-work obligation.
how_to_apply: Secure (or apply for) admission to a doctoral programme abroad.
Register on app.iec.gov.ge during the February–April window and upload CV, motivation, diplomas and research plan.
In stage II, upload the admission letter and tuition/research cost documents.
Sign the grant contract if selected.
iec-doctoral-studies-abroad-grant-2027.costs: Tuition/research fees and living costs up to the ceilings set in the annual call (paid in GEL equivalent).

ilia-state-university-erasmus-exchange-f.about:
Ilia State University (Tbilisi) has Erasmus+ inter-institutional agreements with universities across Europe. Through its annual call, Iliauni bachelor's, master's and doctoral students can study abroad for one or two semesters with full academic recognition; Erasmus+ grants cover travel and a monthly living allowance as set in each agreement.

For the fall semester of 2026/27, applicants submitted a Learning Agreement to the faculty expert by 4 February 2026 and the application by 16 February 2026. A similar call for fall 2027 is expected in January-February 2027; specific partner calls (e.g. consortium places) can appear at other times. Check the IRO pages and contact erasmusplus@iliauni.edu.ge.
highlights: Funded semester at a European partner university
Open to bachelor's, master's and PhD students
Fall 2027 call expected Jan-Feb 2027
ilia-state-university-erasmus-exchange-f.eligibility: Students currently enrolled at Ilia State University (bachelor's, master's, doctoral); partner-specific language and GPA requirements.
how_to_apply: Watch iro.iliauni.edu.ge and Iliauni news for the call
Choose partner universities and prepare a Learning Agreement with your faculty expert
Submit the application and documents by the deadline
Selection; nominated students then apply to the host university
ilia-state-university-erasmus-exchange-f.costs: Erasmus+ grant (travel + monthly allowance) per agreement; tuition waived at the host.

iliauni-summer-school-english-georgian-s.about:
Ilia State University's Summer School of English and Georgian Studies brings international university students to Tbilisi for two weeks each July. The programme combines English-language development at B1 or B2 level with a first introduction to the Georgian language and courses on Georgian history, culture and society, including the country's role in the Black Sea and Caucasus region.

Field trips include a Tbilisi city tour, Kakheti (Sighnaghi and the wine route), Mtskheta (Svetitskhoveli Cathedral and Jvari Monastery), the Ethnographic Museum and the Georgian National Museum. In 2026 it ran from 5 to 19 July on the main campus; the fee was 1,500 USD (5% off for registration by 10 May), covering tuition, materials, two weeks' accommodation, insurance, field trips and some meals. Applicants email summer@iliauni.edu.ge with an ID copy, CV and a recommendation letter from their university.

A compact way to spend part of the summer in Georgia while improving English and earning a certificate from a leading Georgian university.
highlights: English (B1-B2) plus Georgian language and culture
Trips to Kakheti, Mtskheta and museums
Accommodation and insurance included
iliauni-summer-school-english-georgian-s.eligibility: Full-time students at any higher-education institution who have completed at least one semester and are 18+; English at B1-B2. Open to all nationalities.
how_to_apply: Watch the Ilia State University International Relations Office site for the 2027 call (expected spring)
Email summer@iliauni.edu.ge with a copy of your passport/ID, your CV and a recommendation letter from your university
Register by the early-bird date for a 5% discount
Pay the fee and arrange your flight to Tbilisi
iliauni-summer-school-english-georgian-s.costs: 2026 fee: 1,500 USD (tuition, materials, 2 weeks' accommodation, insurance, field trips, some meals). Airfare and personal costs not included.

iset-pmcg-need-based-scholarship-2027.about:
ISET, the International School of Economics at Tbilisi State University, runs the South Caucasus's leading English-taught MA in Economics. The Policy and Management Consulting Group (PMCG), an international consulting firm that employs many ISET graduates, has created a need-based scholarship for MA students who require financial support to continue their studies.

The award is based on financial need rather than academic ranking. ISET also offers CFA Institute student scholarships and a Bank of Georgia partnership for its Master in Finance.
highlights: Need-based support for an English-taught MA in Economics
Funded by an employer of ISET graduates
Strong placement into policy, banking and research jobs
iset-pmcg-need-based-scholarship-2027.eligibility: Students admitted to (or enrolled in) ISET's MA in Economics who can document financial need.
how_to_apply: Apply for admission to ISET's MA in Economics.
Watch iset.ge for the PMCG scholarship call (usually spring).
Submit the scholarship application with evidence of financial need.
Contact ISET admissions for questions.
iset-pmcg-need-based-scholarship-2027.costs: Partial or full tuition support depending on need and the call terms.

ja-georgia-student-company-programme.about:
Junior Achievement (JA) Georgia is the Georgian member of JA Worldwide, the global non-profit that has taught entrepreneurship since 1919. Its Basics of Entrepreneurship (Student Company) programme lets secondary-school pupils experience running a business: they form a mini-company, choose a product or service, raise share capital, produce, market and sell, and then wind the company up and report to shareholders.

The programme is delivered in class by trained teachers in participating schools across Georgia, alongside JA's other in-school modules on financial literacy and workplace readiness (for example 'Be an Entrepreneur' for ages 13-19). JA Georgia also runs one-day Innovation Camps with schools and partners.

Pupils whose school is not yet involved can ask a teacher or the principal to contact JA Georgia (jag@jag.ge, +995 558 56 55 99). It is one of the most recognised school entrepreneurship programmes worldwide.
highlights: Run a real student company for a school year
Part of the global JA Worldwide network
Free for participating schools
ja-georgia-student-company-programme.eligibility: Secondary-school pupils (roughly grades 9-12) in schools taking part in JA Georgia programmes. Georgian-language.
how_to_apply: Ask your teacher or principal whether your school runs JA Georgia programmes
If not, the school contacts JA Georgia at jag@jag.ge or +995 558 56 55 99
Form a student company team with classmates under a trained teacher
Run the company through the school year
ja-georgia-student-company-programme.costs: Free for pupils; schools arrange participation with JA Georgia.

japan-embassy-georgia-japanese-speech-co.about:
The Embassy of Japan in Georgia holds its 4th Japanese Language Speech Contest on Saturday 28 November 2026 (11:00–17:30) in the Auditorium Magnum of Free University of Tbilisi. The general theme is Japanese Culture. It gives learners a stage to show what they have achieved and to meet other students of Japanese.

There are three categories, matched to JLPT/JLCAT levels: beginner (N5–N4 / A1–A2), intermediate (N3 / B1) and advanced (N2–N1 / C1). Each category has two set topics; speeches last 3 minutes, must be delivered from memory, and are followed by questions from the jury in Japanese. Judging covers content (40 points), delivery (30) and answers (30). Winners, runners-up and third places receive certificates of commendation, plus "Good Effort" awards across categories.

If many people apply, the embassy screens applications and may reassign categories; results are emailed on 20 November.
highlights: Free contest run by the Embassy of Japan
Three levels from beginner to advanced
Certificates for top three in each category
japan-embassy-georgia-japanese-speech-co.eligibility: Georgian citizens learning Japanese. In-service Japanese teachers cannot enter. Past winners may only enter a higher category (advanced winners may re-enter advanced). Anyone who studied in Japan for over a year competes in the advanced category.
how_to_apply: Choose your category and one of its two topics
Write your speech manuscript in Japanese and in Georgian (name at the top)
Fill in the online application form linked on the embassy page and upload the manuscript and any JLPT/JLCAT certificate
Submit by 10 November 2026
Wait for the screening result and category confirmation on 20 November

kiu-scholarships-grants-2027.about:
Kutaisi International University opened in 2020 as a special-status public university created with the support of the international charity foundation Cartu, which is investing over €1 billion in the campus. It teaches English-language bachelor's programmes in computer science, management, mathematics and other fields, with partners such as TUM.

For Georgian citizens admitted through the Unified National Exams (or without UNE where allowed), KIU runs an Undergraduate Student Grants Fund comprising KIU Social Grants, KIU Academic Grants, KIU Co-Financing Grants, KIU Institutional Grants and the Rector's Scholarship. International students can apply for 25–50% discounts on KIU housing (EUR 250/month double, EUR 500 single) based on financial need, renewed annually.

A modern residential campus, CERN and TUM links and generous internal funding make KIU one of the best-value options in the region.
highlights: Multiple grant types for Georgian citizens (social, academic, co-financing, Rector's)
25–50% housing discount for international students
English-taught STEM and management degrees with TUM partnership
kiu-scholarships-grants-2027.eligibility: Georgian citizens admitted to KIU bachelor's programmes (grant type depends on UNE results, social status and academic record); international students admitted to KIU with demonstrated financial need for the housing discount.
how_to_apply: Georgian citizens: sit the 2027 UNE and choose KIU; check KIU's grant rules on kiu.edu.ge.
International students: apply for admission (apply@kiu.edu.ge) and complete the Financial Aid form.
Submit the financial-aid form with your justification by 5 August.
Reapply each year for housing discounts.
kiu-scholarships-grants-2027.costs: Grants reduce or cover tuition for Georgian citizens; international students may get 25–50% off housing (EUR 250–500/month).

nbg-global-money-week-banknote-drawing-c.about:
Every March, the National Bank of Georgia's FINEDU platform celebrates Global Money Week with creative competitions for children. In 2026 the theme was "My Region - My Banknote": entrants hand-drew both sides of a banknote representing their city, village or region, including security features such as a serial number and security thread.

It is open to children and teens aged 6-17 in three age groups (6-9, 10-13, 14-17). Entries are posted as a comment on FINEDU's official Facebook competition post (parents submit for under-16s). A jury from the NBG and partner banks picks two winners per age group, plus a public-vote winner; each received 500 GEL plus educational gifts.

The theme changes each year, so check finedu.gov.ge in March 2027.
highlights: Cash prizes (500 GEL per winner in 2026)
Three age groups from 6 to 17
Fun way to learn about money and banknotes
nbg-global-money-week-banknote-drawing-c.eligibility: Children and teenagers aged 6-17 (2026 rules). Prizes are paid into a bank account in Georgia. Entries in Georgian context.
how_to_apply: Check finedu.gov.ge events in March 2027 for the theme and rules
Create a hand-made artwork (no digital or AI images)
Post a clear photo as a comment on the official FINEDU Facebook competition post with name and age (parent submits for under-16s)
nbg-global-money-week-banknote-drawing-c.costs: Free. Prizes paid by the National Bank of Georgia and partner banks.

nbg-regulators-dilemma-student-competiti.about:
"Regulator's Dilemma" is the National Bank of Georgia's annual student competition, run through its FINEDU financial-education platform with support from Credo Bank. Teams receive a real dilemma from central-bank work, analyse it and present practical recommendations to a jury of at least three NBG experts.

Teams of 3-6 bachelor or master students from the same authorised Georgian university register online; only the first 20 teams get into round one. Five teams reach the final round and three winners share prizes of 4,000, 2,000 and 1,500 GEL (split among members). In 2026 registration was 19-25 October, round one 16-17 November and the final on 7 December.

It is an excellent way for economics, finance and law students to understand monetary policy and supervision and to get noticed by the central bank.
highlights: Work on a real central-bank policy dilemma
Present to NBG experts; prizes up to 4,000 GEL
Strong CV signal for economics/finance careers
nbg-regulators-dilemma-student-competiti.eligibility: Teams of 3-6 students enrolled in bachelor or master programmes at the same authorised higher education institution in Georgia (members may be from different years and faculties). Working language Georgian.
how_to_apply: Watch finedu.gov.ge events in early October 2027 for the call
Form a team of 3-6 students from your university
Register via the online form as soon as registration opens (first 20 teams only)
Solve the first-round assignment and email it to info@finedu.gov.ge
Present to the jury; finalists get a second assignment

olyinfo-georgian-school-informatics-olym.about:
OLYINFO is the national school olympiad in informatics run by the Georgian Tech Olympiads Hub, a joint project of TBC Bank and the Business and Technology University (BTU) that selects and trains Georgia's teams for EJOI, EGOI, IOI and the International Olympiad in AI. It aims to improve informatics teaching across the country and give gifted pupils free learning resources and camps.

Pupils in grades 3-12 at Georgian schools compete in four age groups (III-IV, V-VI, VII-VIII and IX-XII) on logic and algorithm problems suited to their age. Round 1 is online; the final is held in person on the BTU campus in Tbilisi, where 40 winners (10 per age group) are selected. Registration is by a Google form that TBC posts on its education site; in the last cycle it ran from 26 December to 29 January.

For younger pupils it is the most accessible entry point into Georgia's competitive-programming pipeline.
highlights: Four age groups from grade 3 to grade 12
Online first round, final at BTU
Winners gain free training and camps
olyinfo-georgian-school-informatics-olym.eligibility: Pupils in grades 3-12 at general-education schools in Georgia.
how_to_apply: Check the OLYINFO page on tbcbank.ge from late December 2026
Fill in the Google registration form before the deadline (last cycle: 29 January)
Sit the online first round
If qualified, attend the final at the BTU campus in Tbilisi

pan-caucasian-youth-orchestra-2027.about:
The Pan-Caucasian Youth Orchestra was founded in 2019 and is resident at the Tsinandali Festival in Kakheti, eastern Georgia. Each summer selected young musicians spend about four weeks in Tsinandali: seating auditions, coaching and sectionals with international tutors, full-orchestra rehearsals with Maestro Gianandrea Noseda, then four concerts at the festival (the 2026 cycle ran 15 August-14 September).

It is for orchestral musicians aged 18-28 born in Georgia or the region; the FAQ lists Armenia, Azerbaijan, Georgia, Kazakhstan, Turkey, Turkmenistan, Ukraine and Uzbekistan. Younger players can ask for permission to audition. Applicants submit an online form and give a roughly 10-minute audition (solo pieces plus listed orchestral excerpts); results come about a week after auditions end.

The festival covers travel to Tsinandali, shared accommodation and meals, with no fee to apply or take part, which makes it one of the most valuable orchestral experiences for young musicians in the Caucasus.
highlights: Travel, accommodation and meals covered; no fees
Work with Gianandrea Noseda and international coaches
Four concerts at one of the region's leading classical festivals
pan-caucasian-youth-orchestra-2027.eligibility: Orchestral musicians aged 18-28 with some orchestra experience, born in Georgia or another eligible country of the region (Armenia, Azerbaijan, Kazakhstan, Turkey, Turkmenistan, Ukraine, Uzbekistan). Under-18s must request permission (sonja@tsfest.ge).
how_to_apply: Read the audition programme and FAQ on pcyo.tsinandalifestival.ge
Fill in the online application when the 2027 call opens and choose your audition date
Prepare one or two pieces plus the listed orchestral excerpts (bring your own pianist if needed)
Attend the audition (or request a remote format by email); results arrive about a week after auditions close
pan-caucasian-youth-orchestra-2027.costs: Free to apply. If selected, travel to and from Tsinandali, accommodation and meals are covered. Health, accident and instrument insurance are your own responsibility.

rustaveli-bachelor-student-research-gran.about:
The Bachelor's Student Grant (BSG) competition is run by the Shota Rustaveli National Science Foundation of Georgia to support students' scientific interests, innovative ideas and research skills, and their involvement in education and science popularisation. Each project can request up to 15,000 GEL.

A project needs a project leader and at least three main personnel, who must be Georgian citizens and active students on an accredited bachelor's programme at a Georgian higher-education institution. They apply through a lead organisation: a Georgian university, a public-law entity or a registered Georgian non-profit. Projects are registered in the Foundation's GMUS system between 30 October and 13 November 2026 (18:00), and the signed participation application goes to the Foundation by 17 November 2026. Online consultations are held on 3 and 10 November at 16:00; results and grant agreements are due in December 2026.

For undergraduates this is a rare chance to lead a funded research project of their own, which carries real weight in master's and PhD applications.
highlights: Up to 15,000 GEL per student-led project
Teams of 3+ bachelor's students with a host institution
Free online consultations on 3 and 10 November
rustaveli-bachelor-student-research-gran.eligibility: Georgian citizens enrolled as active students on an accredited bachelor's programme at a higher-education institution in Georgia; at least three main personnel plus a project leader; applied for through a Georgian university, public-law entity or non-profit.
how_to_apply: Read the call and Annex 1 conditions on rustaveli.org.ge
Agree a lead organisation (usually your university) and a consultant
Register the project in GMUS (gmus.rustaveli.org.ge) by 13 November 2026, 18:00, with proposal, schedule, budget and student-status certificates
Submit the signed participation application to the Foundation's chancellery by 17 November 2026, 18:00
Questions: bsg@rustaveli.org.ge
rustaveli-bachelor-student-research-gran.costs: Grant of up to 15,000 GEL per project; no application fee.

rustaveli-foundation-bachelor-student-re.about:
The Shota Rustaveli National Science Foundation's 2026 targeted grant competition for bachelor's students supports undergraduates enrolled in accredited bachelor's programmes in Georgia: it aims to spark and reward their scientific interests, identify innovative ideas and creative approaches and build research potential.

Applications are institutional: the student team (key personnel, who must be Georgian citizens studying in Georgia) applies together with a lead organisation such as their university. The amount requested from the Foundation may not exceed GEL 15,000 per project. Projects are registered online in the Foundation's GMUS system.
highlights: Up to GEL 15,000 for an undergraduate-led research project
Open now: registration closes 13 November 2026
Builds a research CV for master's and PhD applications abroad
rustaveli-foundation-bachelor-student-re.eligibility: Bachelor's students enrolled in accredited programmes at Georgian higher education institutions, who are Georgian citizens, applying together with a lead (host) organisation.
how_to_apply: Agree a project idea and supervisor with your university (lead organisation).
Register the project electronically in GMUS (gmus.rustaveli.org.ge) between 30 Oct and 13 Nov 2026, 18:00.
Submit the signed participation declaration to the Foundation's office by 17 Nov 2026, 18:00.
Await expert evaluation and results on rustaveli.org.ge.
rustaveli-foundation-bachelor-student-re.costs: Project funding up to GEL 15,000 (research costs and remuneration of key personnel per Foundation rules).

rustaveli-leonardo-da-vinci-pupil-invent.about:
The Leonardo da Vinci competition (LEO) is the Shota Rustaveli National Science Foundation's annual contest for school inventors and young researchers. Its aim is to encourage pupils' interest in learning, innovation and technology and to build creative thinking and practical skills.

Pupils in grades 7-12 at any Georgian state or private school can enter alone or in a group of up to three. In stage 1 (registration in spring, through the Foundation's GMUS system) they submit an initial idea or research plan; selected projects go to stage 2 (autumn), where they submit a full description and a physical drawing, model or mock-up. Finalists present at an exhibition in November-December, where winners are chosen and prize money is paid. In 2026 the call opened on 10 March with stage-1 registration from 16 March to 24 April; expect a similar timetable in 2027.

It is the main national science-fair-style competition for Georgian pupils and a strong addition to any STEM university application.
highlights: National exhibition and cash prizes
Individual or teams of up to 3 pupils
Free online consultations during registration
rustaveli-leonardo-da-vinci-pupil-invent.eligibility: Pupils in grades 7-12 at Georgian state or private general-education schools; individual or group (max 3).
how_to_apply: Watch rustaveli.org.ge 'current competitions' for the 2027 call (expected March 2027)
Register in GMUS and upload the initial research plan, project summary and consent form
Submit the physical participation application to the Foundation
If selected, submit the full project description and model in stage 2 (September)
Present at the final exhibition (November-December)
rustaveli-leonardo-da-vinci-pupil-invent.costs: Free to enter; prize money for winners.

sangu-davitianni-intellectual-olympiad-2.about:
The youth movement 'Davitianni', in cooperation with St. Andrew the First-Called Georgian University (SANGU) in Tbilisi, is running the university intellectual olympiad 'Get to Know Abkhazia, Protect the Heritage'. Registration is open until 6 November 2026 through the form linked on SANGU's announcement.

The olympiad has three stages: a team qualifying round in crossword format (teams of 2-3 students), an individual round with a test, and a team final that decides first, second and third places. Every participant receives a certificate and scholarship points, and the winning teams go on to compete in a grand final on behalf of SANGU.

It suits SANGU students who enjoy quiz-style competitions and Georgian history, and offers scholarship points as a tangible reward.
highlights: Team and individual rounds
Certificate and scholarship points for every participant
Winners advance to a grand final
sangu-davitianni-intellectual-olympiad-2.eligibility: Students of St. Andrew the First-Called Georgian University (SANGU), in teams of 2-3. Conducted in Georgian.
how_to_apply: Form a team of 2-3 SANGU students
Register through the form linked on SANGU's announcement by 6 November 2026
Take part in the crossword qualifying round, the individual test and the team final

sangu-nku-cybersecurity-masters-full-fun.about:
St. Andrew the First-Called Georgian University of the Patriarchate of Georgia (SANGU) runs a master's programme in cybersecurity jointly with Northern Kentucky University (USA). Graduates receive a dual degree: Master of Science in Cybersecurity from SANGU and from NKU.

The annual tuition is listed as fully funded. The programme lasts two years (at least 120 ECTS). Applicants must pass Georgia's Common Master's Exam plus the programme's own requirements.
highlights: Free tuition for a US–Georgian dual master's degree
Cybersecurity, a high-demand field
Study in Tbilisi with American curriculum
sangu-nku-cybersecurity-masters-full-fun.eligibility: Bachelor's degree holders eligible for Georgia's Common Master's Exams (Georgian citizens and eligible residents), meeting SANGU/NKU English and programme requirements.
how_to_apply: Register for the 2027 Common Master's Exam with NAEC.
Meet SANGU's internal exam/interview and English requirements.
Apply to the SANGU cybersecurity master's programme.
Enrol in autumn 2027.

tbc-campus-free-business-courses-2027.about:
TBC Campus is a free programme from TBC Bank, delivered with partner Colab, for university students interested in business careers. Four modules rotate through the year: Marketing (digital marketing, ad content, SEO), Technologies & Data (tech project management, data analysis, IT business analysis, SQL), Business (entrepreneurship, business planning, investment finance) and Product (product management, UI/UX, product design and CX strategy).

Courses run online on Google Meet twice a week for two hours and last one to three months; certificates go to those who complete assignments and a final project. Selection has two stages: the registration form with a first assignment, then a second assignment by email; registration order also counts. You may apply to several courses but take only one. In the last cycle Marketing registration ran 27 January-5 February.

A free, practical way for students anywhere in Georgia to build job-ready skills and a portfolio project.
highlights: Free; taught by industry professionals
Marketing, data, business and product tracks
Certificate and final project
tbc-campus-free-business-courses-2027.eligibility: Students aged 18-24 from anywhere in Georgia; internet and a mid-range computer needed. Georgian-language.
how_to_apply: Open the TBC Campus page and pick the module that is open
Fill in the registration form including the first-stage assignment
Complete the second-stage assignment sent by email
If selected, attend twice-weekly online lectures

tbc-crash-courses-for-girls-2027.about:
TBC Tech School's Crash Courses for Girls are short summer courses that introduce girls to technology. There are four tracks: Introduction to Artificial Intelligence, Introduction to Mobile App Development, Web Programming Back-End (Python and Flask), and Web Programming Front-End (HTML and CSS).

Each course runs online on Google Meet for two weeks, three two-hour sessions a week (six lectures, 12 hours). Before applying, candidates complete a short assignment for their chosen track (explained in a video) and submit it with the registration form; selection weighs the form, the assignment, regional balance and registration order. Completing assignments and a final project earns a certificate. Participants can take one course.

The courses are fully funded by TBC and open to girls from any region of Georgia, making them an easy first step into coding before university.
highlights: Free, fully online, any region
Four tracks: AI, mobile, back-end, front-end
Certificate on completion
tbc-crash-courses-for-girls-2027.eligibility: Girls in grades 9-12 (FAQ says X-XI priority) at schools in Georgia; internet access and a computer or phone needed. Georgian-language.
how_to_apply: Watch the Crash Courses page on tbcbank.ge for the summer 2027 dates
Watch the track's assignment video and complete the task
Submit the registration form with your assignment
Wait for the selection email

tbc-it-academy-2027.about:
TBC IT Academy is a free, TBC-funded training programme that prepares people for careers in technology. Courses include Quality Engineering and Test Automation, Android Development, .NET, Blockchain Technologies, GetData (data), Frontend Development, iOS Development and IT Support Fundamentals.

Courses are online, in Georgian, usually in the evenings, last three to six months and take about 20-30 students each. Selection is competitive: online skills test, technical test or assignment, an HR motivation video and a technical interview. Graduates get a certificate and the strongest may be offered jobs at TBC and its subsidiaries. TBC states that registration for most courses opens in the autumn; the current intake is closed.

One of the best-known free routes into software careers in Georgia, worth tracking for the next intake.
highlights: 100% funded by TBC Bank
8 tracks from Android to blockchain
Possible employment at TBC
tbc-it-academy-2027.eligibility: Anyone aged 18+ who wants to work in IT; Georgian-language instruction.
how_to_apply: Watch the TBC IT Academy page for the next intake
Register for one or more courses within the deadline
Pass the online skills test and technical test
Submit the HR video and pass the technical interview

tbc-risk-academy-2027.about:
TBC Risk Academy is an intensive, roughly four-month programme from TBC Bank that teaches analytical skills and the fundamentals of risk management through practical and theoretical training led by sector specialists. Modules cover Excel 365 (data cleaning, pivot tables, modelling, Solver), SQL (joins, CTEs, views, procedures), Power BI (Power Query, data modelling, DAX) and data analytics (dashboard design, Databricks and AI in analytics, final project), plus meetings with heads of TBC's risk departments.

Classes are hybrid, two to three times a week, mostly in the evenings, with an in-person test after each subject. Forty participants are split into two groups (last cycle: 8 September-25 December and 4 November-10 March). Selection runs in spring: web registration (27 April-15 May in the last cycle), an online info day, an in-person test on probability, Excel and logic, a video interview, and an assignment presented to TBC's risk team. Everyone admitted is 100% funded and receives a certificate on completion.

Ideal for third- and fourth-year students or graduates in economics, maths or business who want a data-analytics career.
highlights: 100% funded by TBC Bank
Excel, SQL, Power BI and analytics
Meet TBC's risk leadership
tbc-risk-academy-2027.eligibility: Anyone aged 18+ (typically final-year students or recent graduates) motivated to study analytics; no risk-management experience needed. Georgian-language.
how_to_apply: Watch the TBC Risk Academy page from April 2027
Register online within the window (last cycle: 27 April-15 May)
Attend the online info day and pass the in-person test
Complete the video interview and the assignment presentation

tbilisi-american-corner-clubs-2026-27.about:
The Tbilisi American Corner, located in the National Palace of Youth on Rustaveli Avenue, is part of the US Embassy-supported network of American Spaces. For 2026-27 it runs 15 clubs for members in grades 5-12: English for Kids (grades 5-6), American Book Club (7-8), All About America and Conversation Club (9-12), STEM Club (9-12), Coding Club (6-7), Robotics (5-6), 3D Printing Club (9-12), American Government Club (9-11), movie clubs, a board-games club and an SAT Math Program for grade 11.

Membership is by online registration, which opened on 15 September 2026; clubs meet weekly through the school year. The page lists no fees. Questions go to +995 599 899 755 or info@nationalpalace.ge.

Especially useful for pupils preparing for US universities (SAT Math, English conversation) or wanting hands-on STEM and 3D printing.
highlights: SAT Math programme for grade 11
STEM, coding, robotics and 3D printing
English conversation and American studies clubs
tbilisi-american-corner-clubs-2026-27.eligibility: Pupils in grades 5-12 (each club has its own grade range). Clubs run mainly in English.
how_to_apply: Open the Tbilisi American Corner page on youthpalace.ge
Fill in the membership registration form linked there
Choose clubs that match your grade
Attend weekly at the National Palace of Youth, 6 Rustaveli Avenue
tbilisi-american-corner-clubs-2026-27.costs: No fee is listed on the page; confirm when registering.

tedx-british-university-georgia-2026.about:
TEDxBritish University Georgia is an independently organised TEDx event licensed by TED and listed in TED's official TEDx events directory as a 'University' event. It takes place on 27 November 2026 in Tbilisi, organised by Levan Gurgenidze, with the organiser address at 92 Vepkhistkaosani Street, Tbilisi.

TEDx university events combine short live talks by students, academics and local professionals with recorded TED Talks, followed by networking. TED lists this event as open to the public, so secondary-school and university students can attend as audience members; speaker and volunteer places are decided by the organising team.

It is a low-barrier way to hear new ideas, meet people from Tbilisi's university community and, for those who want to speak, a chance to get on the path to giving a TEDx talk.
highlights: Official TEDx event licensed by TED
Open to the public according to TED's listing
Talks by students, academics and local professionals
tedx-british-university-georgia-2026.eligibility: Open to the public. Best suited to university and senior secondary-school students in Tbilisi; most talks are expected in English or Georgian.
how_to_apply: Open the event's page on ted.com (TEDx events, Georgia) to confirm the date and venue
Contact the organising team listed on the TED page (or the host school/university) to ask for a seat
If you want to speak or volunteer, ask the organisers about speaker and volunteer calls well before the date
Arrive on the day with your confirmation; talks may later be published on the TEDx YouTube channel
tedx-british-university-georgia-2026.costs: TED's listing does not mention a ticket price; TEDx university events are usually free or low-cost. Confirm with the organisers. Travel is at your own cost.

tedx-buckswood-tbilisi-2027.about:
TEDxBuckswood Intl School Tbilisi is a TEDx 'Youth' event, licensed by TED, held at Buckswood International School, 156 Rustaveli Street, Tskneti (Tbilisi). TED's official events directory lists it for 28 March 2027, organised by Megi Kldiashvili.

In the TEDx Youth format, secondary-school students research, write and rehearse short talks and present them alongside invited speakers. The event is marked as open to the public, so students from other schools can come to watch and network.

With the date set months ahead, it is also a realistic target for students who want to ask the organisers about volunteering or speaking opportunities.
highlights: TEDx Youth event at an international boarding school
Date fixed well in advance: 28 March 2027
Open to the public according to TED
tedx-buckswood-tbilisi-2027.eligibility: Open to the public; aimed at secondary-school students. Speaker places are decided by the organising team.
how_to_apply: Open the event's page on ted.com (TEDx events, Georgia) to confirm the date and venue
Contact the organising team listed on the TED page (or the host school/university) to ask for a seat
If you want to speak or volunteer, ask the organisers about speaker and volunteer calls well before the date
Arrive on the day with your confirmation; talks may later be published on the TEDx YouTube channel
tedx-buckswood-tbilisi-2027.costs: No ticket price is published on TED's listing; school TEDx Youth events are normally free. Confirm with the school.

tedx-ib-european-school-tbilisi-2026.about:
TEDxIB European School is a TEDx 'Youth' event, licensed by TED, hosted by the European School in Tbilisi (2 Irine Skhirtladze Street), an International Baccalaureate school. TED's official events directory lists it for 20 November 2026, organised by Keti Nachkebia with co-organiser Tea Siradze.

TEDx Youth events put school students on stage: pupils prepare and deliver short talks, often coached by teachers, alongside guest speakers. The event is listed as open to the public, so students from other schools and families can attend.

For a secondary-school student it is a chance to see peers give polished talks in English, and a model for anyone thinking of starting a TEDx Youth licence at their own school.
highlights: TEDx Youth format: school students on stage
Hosted by an IB World School in Tbilisi
Open to the public according to TED
tedx-ib-european-school-tbilisi-2026.eligibility: Open to the public; aimed at secondary-school students and their families. Speaker slots are usually reserved for students of the host school.
how_to_apply: Open the event's page on ted.com (TEDx events, Georgia) to confirm the date and venue
Contact the organising team listed on the TED page (or the host school/university) to ask for a seat
If you want to speak or volunteer, ask the organisers about speaker and volunteer calls well before the date
Arrive on the day with your confirmation; talks may later be published on the TEDx YouTube channel
tedx-ib-european-school-tbilisi-2026.costs: No ticket price is published on TED's listing; school TEDx Youth events are normally free. Confirm with the school.

tedx-tbilisi-green-school-youth-2027.about:
TEDxTbilisi Green School Youth is a TEDx 'Youth' event, licensed by TED, hosted by Green School Dighomi (3A Evgeni Mikeladze Street, Tbilisi). TED's official events directory lists it for 15 May 2027 from 10:00 to 15:00, organised by Bakur Sulakauri with co-organiser Inga Mdivani.

The TEDx Youth format gives secondary-school students the stage for short, rehearsed talks alongside invited speakers, in a half-day programme. TED marks the event as open to the public.

It suits pupils who want to watch peers speak, practise English and public-speaking skills, or ask the organisers about joining as a volunteer or speaker.
